🤖 How the AI step works here

In this prototype the vision step is simulated on the client (sample-photo profiles + filename/description keywords) so it runs anywhere. The full product calls a vision-capable AI API via POST /ai/analyze. Either way, the rules are the same:

  • AI output is a suggestion, never a verified finding
  • Confidence below 70% → flagged needs human review
  • The citizen can always correct the category
  • Severity is an estimate — not an engineering assessment

🔁 Duplicate logic (MVP)

A possible match = same or related category (Pothole ↔ Road Damage, Waterlogging ↔ Drainage) and same ward or within ~300 m and reported in the last 14 days and still open. Matches are flagged, never silently discarded — you choose: support the existing ticket or file separately.

📩 Report delivery — Gmail + Google Sheet

Gmail is the store for now. Every submitted ticket — from anyone using this page — is sent automatically to the connected Google Apps Script web app in the project owner's Google account, which (1) appends a row to the CityPulse Reports Google Sheet and (2) sends an email to hariteja.ch@gmail.com with the ticket details and the photo attached.

Delivery status: ✅ Connected. Every new submission from any visitor is posted automatically to the connected Apps Script endpoint — creating a row in the Google Sheet and an email to hariteja.ch@gmail.com with the photo attached (when a photo was uploaded).

Apps Script receiver — deployed & connected (the live code)
  1. ✅ The CityPulse Reports Google Sheet exists in the owner's Google account, with the code below in its Apps Script project (Extensions → Apps Script).
  2. ✅ Deployed as a Web app — execute as “Me”, access “Anyone” — and its URL is wired into this page above.
  3. Every submission from any visitor now creates a row in the Sheet's Reports tab and an email to hariteja.ch@gmail.com with the photo attached (photos are also saved to the owner's Drive).
  4. If the script is ever redeployed, paste the new Web App URL above and tap Update endpoint.
var SHEET_NAME = 'Reports';
var INBOX = 'hariteja.ch@gmail.com';

var HEADERS = [
  'Ticket No', 'Submitted At', 'Name', 'Phone',
  'Category', 'Ward / Area', 'Location', 'Description',
  'AI Category', 'AI Confidence', 'Severity', 'Status',
  'Photo File Name', 'Photo Drive Link'
];

function doGet() {
  return ContentService
    .createTextOutput(JSON.stringify({ ok: true, service: 'CityPulse AI report receiver' }))
    .setMimeType(ContentService.MimeType.JSON);
}

function doPost(e) {
  try {
    var data = JSON.parse(e.postData.contents);

    var ss = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSpreadsheet();
    var sheet = ss.getSheetByName(SHEET_NAME);
    if (!sheet) {
      sheet = ss.insertSheet(SHEET_NAME);
    }
    if (sheet.getLastRow() === 0) {
      sheet.appendRow(HEADERS);
    }

    var photoName = data.photoName || '';
    var photoLink = '';
    var photoBlob = null;
    if (data.photoBase64) {
      var base64 = String(data.photoBase64).split(',').pop();
      photoBlob = Utilities.newBlob(
        Utilities.base64Decode(base64),
        data.photoType || 'image/jpeg',
        photoName || 'photo.jpg'
      );
      var file = DriveApp.createFile(photoBlob);
      photoLink = file.getUrl();
    }

    sheet.appendRow([
      data.ticketNo || '',
      data.submittedAt || new Date().toISOString(),
      data.name || '',
      data.phone || '',
      data.category || '',
      data.ward || '',
      data.location || '',
      data.description || '',
      data.aiCategory || '',
      data.aiConfidence === undefined ? '' : data.aiConfidence,
      data.severity || '',
      data.status || 'SUBMITTED',
      photoName,
      photoLink
    ]);

    var subject = 'CityPulse AI report ' + (data.ticketNo || '') +
      ' — ' + (data.category || 'Report') + ' (' + (data.ward || '') + ')';
    var body =
      'New CityPulse AI report\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Ticket: ' + (data.ticketNo || '') + '\n' +
      'Category: ' + (data.category || '') + '\n' +
      'Ward / Area: ' + (data.ward || '') + '\n' +
      'Location: ' + (data.location || '') + '\n' +
      'Description: ' + (data.description || '') + '\n' +
      'AI suggestion: ' + (data.aiCategory || '') +
      ' (' + (data.aiConfidence === undefined ? '' : data.aiConfidence) + '% confidence, severity ' +
      (data.severity || '') + ')\n' +
      'Status: ' + (data.status || 'SUBMITTED') + '\n' +
      'Reported by: ' + (data.name || 'Citizen') + ' ' + (data.phone || '') + '\n' +
      'Submitted: ' + (data.submittedAt || '') + '\n' +
      'Photo: ' + (photoLink || 'No photo attached') + '\n' +
      '\n' +
      'This report is also saved in the CityPulse Reports Google Sheet.';

    var options = { name: 'CityPulse AI' };
    if (photoBlob) {
      options.attachments = [photoBlob];
    }
    GmailApp.sendEmail(INBOX, subject, body, options);

    return ContentService
      .createTextOutput(JSON.stringify({ ok: true, ticket: data.ticketNo || '' }))
      .setMimeType(ContentService.MimeType.JSON);
  } catch (err) {
    return ContentService
      .createTextOutput(JSON.stringify({ ok: false, error: String(err) }))
      .setMimeType(ContentService.MimeType.JSON);
  }
}

Featured issue · Bachupally

🌫️ Air pollution & chemical-factory fumes — Bachupally

Residents of Bachupally have repeatedly reported that this is not regular traffic pollution alone — it is the combination of industrial emissions, chemical odours, dust and nearby industrial activity affecting residential zones. This concern is seeded in the app as ticket CP-2026-0016 (category: Air Pollution, ward: Bachupally) — find it on the map and in Track.

What residents report

  • Chemical odours / fumes, especially during evening and night hours
  • Air pollution allegedly originating from nearby industrial areas — IDA Bollaram, Kazipally, Bonthapally, Jinnaram, Pashamylaram and Sultanpur — which have several pharma and chemical manufacturing units
  • Dust pollution from ongoing construction, road works and heavy traffic
  • Complaints of headaches, respiratory discomfort, sinus issues and eye irritation associated with the foul-smelling emissions
  • Industrial air emissions and chemical fumes near residential areas
  • Possible groundwater contamination in some locations near residential areas

If you notice strong chemical smells

  • Report it to the Telangana Pollution Control Board (TGPCB) with the exact time, location and duration
  • Take photos / videos if visible emissions are present
  • Coordinate with your apartment association or welfare association — collective complaints typically receive more attention
  • Log it here too: note the time and duration in the description so a pattern builds up, report by report

Resident-reported concern, presented as reported — sources of emissions are alleged by residents, not verified by this app. Reports here are unverified until reviewed.

🌧️ Rainwater harvesting — what your roof can catch

Simple maths: roof area (m²) × rainfall (cm) × 10 = litres of rain that can be captured or sent into a recharge pit instead of flooding the lane.

💧 This rain could give you about 2,000 litres — enough to recharge groundwater through a pit instead of adding to drainage overflow.

Illustrative estimate from the formula above (before losses). Report a missing or broken harvesting pit in your building from the Report form — category “Rainwater Harvesting” — and it becomes a tracked ticket.

📚 Educating about water usage

🚰 Fix the dripA leaking tap or flush quietly wastes water every single day — one repair visit beats a month of tanker orders.
🪣 Bucket over showerBathing with a bucket uses far less than a long shower; keep a mug for shaving and brushing instead of a running tap.
🌱 Reuse RO reject waterWater from the RO purifier's reject pipe is fine for mopping, flushing and watering plants — don't send it down the drain.
🚗 Wash smartA bucket and cloth for the car instead of a hose pipe; wash on the lawn or gravel so water soaks in, not onto the road.
🏢 Community checksApartment associations: audit common-area taps, borewell recharge pits and harvesting structures before the monsoon, not after the first flood.

Share your own tip in the Community Feed — good habits spread neighbour to neighbour.

About the product

Problem, architecture & honest scope

Honest scope: this page is a fully interactive prototype of the complete CityPulse AI journey. The GitHub repo carries the full-stack implementation (Next.js + FastAPI + Supabase) built to the same design — the two share the same data model, API contract and workflow.

🔍 Problem & research

Hyderabad residents face potholes, garbage, dark streets, waterlogging and congestion daily — but reporting is fragmented and citizens rarely learn what happened to a complaint, so they stop reporting. Street intercepts and an online survey with shopkeepers, auto drivers and residents' associations (a small local sample, not city statistics) found "no update after reporting" was the top frustration, and photo proof of progress mattered more than promises.

💡 Solution

Most civic apps stop at collecting complaints. CityPulse AI adds intelligence (AI category suggestion with confidence + human-review gate), quality validation (duplicate detection that flags, never discards), and transparent tracking (unique ticket, public map, append-only status history) — so citizens can see whether issues are being reviewed and what happens next.

🏗️ Architecture

  • Frontend: Next.js · React · TypeScript · Tailwind — citizen + admin apps
  • Backend: FastAPI · Pydantic — versioned REST API, RBAC, workflow rules
  • Data: Supabase PostgreSQL + Storage — complaints, locations, ai_analysis, duplicate_matches, status_history, citizen_points
  • Maps: Leaflet + OpenStreetMap (live in this prototype)
  • AI: vision-capable API behind POST /ai/analyze
  • Hosting: Vercel (web) + Render (API)

🔌 API contract · /api/v1

  • POST /complaints · GET /complaints · GET /complaints/{id}
  • POST /complaints/{id}/media — image upload
  • POST /ai/analyze — predicted_category, confidence, suggested_severity, visible_evidence, needs_human_review
  • GET /complaints/{id}/duplicates
  • PATCH /admin/complaints/{id}/status — admin only
  • GET /map/issues · GET /analytics/overview · GET /leaderboard

🔄 Status workflow

SUBMITTED → UNDER REVIEW → VERIFIED → IN PROGRESS → RESOLVED

Rejected and Duplicate-merged are separate outcomes and must include a reason. Transitions are enforced (in production, server-side); citizens view progress but cannot change status. Every transition is appended to status_history with actor, remarks and timestamp.

⚠️ Limitations & responsible claims

  • Citizen reports are unverified until reviewed — verification state is always shown
  • AI severity is an estimate, never an engineering assessment; AI never infers ownership or legal responsibility from a photo
  • All data here is demo data; no government affiliation, no live official statuses
  • Faces and number plates must be blurred before any photo is published
  • Prototype limits: simulated AI, in-browser storage, demo admin role (production enforces Supabase Auth + backend RBAC)

🌍 Impact

When reporting visibly leads somewhere, citizens keep reporting. Wards get fair, data-backed priorities; repeat hotspots (the same drain, the same dark corner) become patterns instead of anecdotes; and admins get a quality loop — AI corrections and duplicate outcomes — that makes the system smarter with every review.
